Content (2 marks): heading and byline; date; speaker; key ideas; students' questions; response. Expression (2 marks): fluency, accuracy of grammar and spelling, appropriate register and word limit.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In 'The Adventure', Gaitonde was astonished by the Bombay he saw.
Reason (R): Bombay looked exactly as he had always known it.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true, but R is false; in fact, history had taken a different course there after the Marathas won at Panipat.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the story 'The Adventure', and answer.

"'Think of a pencil balanced on its point,' the scientist said. 'The smallest breath of air decides which way it falls. History has such moments too. On that field in 1761, one bullet passing a few inches to the left might have sent our country down another road.' His friend, the historian, said nothing for a long time."

Answer the following:
(i) What does the balanced pencil illustrate?  (a) Air is heavy  (b) A small cause can decide a large outcome  (c) Gravity is weak  (d) Pencils are useless
(ii) Which battle is meant by "that field in 1761"?  (a) The Battle of Plassey  (b) The third Battle of Panipat  (c) The first Battle of Panipat  (d) The Battle of Buxar
(iii) What might have happened if the bullet had missed?
(iv) Why did the historian say nothing for a long time?
items.answer: (i) (b) A small cause can decide a large outcome (ii) (b) The third Battle of Panipat (iii) Vishwasrao might have survived and the Marathas might have won, changing history. (iv) He was deeply thinking about the idea that history could have been different.
items.markingKey: (i) (b) A small cause can decide a large outcome (ii) (b) The third Battle of Panipat (iii) Vishwasrao might have survived and the Marathas might have won, changing history. (iv) He was deeply thinking about the idea that history could have been different. (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
